analysis.evidence: God promises Abram that he will bless מְבָרְכֶיךָ, “those who bless you.” The parallel promise אָאֹר, “I will curse,” confirms that God is the one who acts in response to how people treat Abram.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ means “and.” The verb is a Piel first-person common singular cohortative, marked by the first-person prefix אֲ־ and the ending ־ָה. It expresses the speaker’s resolve.
analysis.sense: to confer divine blessing on a person

analysis.evidence: In וַאֲבָרֲכָה מְבָרְכֶיךָ, God promises to bless the people who bless Abram. The parallel וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר contrasts them with the person who curses him.
analysis.morphology: The Piel active participle is masculine plural in the construct state and functions as a noun meaning “those who bless.” The second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ supplies its object, Abram.
analysis.sense: to speak a blessing upon another person
